title: Arizona Public Service Company 2026 to 2035 Ten-Year Transmission System Plan (ACC filing, with Attachments B, C, E, F)
publisher: Arizona Public Service Company (filed with Arizona Corporation Commission, Docket E-99999A-25-0006)
summary: APS's current ten-year plan, filed Jan 30, 2026 (119 pp). Totals: ~72 mi new 500 kV, 1 mi new 345 kV, 578 mi 345 kV rebuilds, 190 mi new 230 kV, 146 mi 230 kV rebuilds, 34 new transformers, $6.2B. Includes 23 project sheets, Table 2 equipment by year, a TBD project table (8 new 500 kV concepts), EHV/Phoenix/Yuma maps, a DG/EE study (2030), the RTAP, a Phoenix load-pocket RMR study 2026-2035 with Phoenix-area load forecast, and planning guidelines. The Technical Study Report, Extreme Contingency Study and ratings are CEII (not filed publicly). Several substations renamed (TS21->Independence, TS22->Wafer, TS33->Helios); many dates pulled forward.

findings.statement: Plan totals: ~72 mi new 500kV OH, ~1 mi new 345kV OH, ~578 mi 345kV OH rebuilds, ~190 mi new 230kV OH, ~146 mi 230kV OH rebuilds, ~1 mi new 230kV UG, ~8 mi 230kV UG upgrades, ~1 mi 115kV rebuild; 34 new transformers, 2 replacements, 4 new series reactors, 15 new shunt capacitors, 1 shunt reactor replacement, 2 series capacitor replacements; total investment $6.2 billion (narrative says 2 new shunt reactors, Table 1 says 3).

Placed in service in 2025: Goodyear 230kV Lines, Parkway 230kV Lines, Broadway 230kV Lines, Dromedary 230kV Lines, Ironwood Solar and Storage 500kV Interconnection, West Camp Wind Gen-Tie (Sitgreaves 345kV switchyard).

Renames: TS33 -> Helios (Sundance-Milligan becomes Helios-Milligan); TS22 -> Wafer; TS21 -> Independence; Runway Additional 230kV Lines -> Diamond 230kV Lines (Diamond-Runway section becomes TBD); TS39 switchyard added on Contrail lines (TBD).

Date changes vs the 2025 plan: Jojoba-Rudd 500kV 2032->2031; Runway-Stratus cut-in to Independence and Independence-Broadway 2032->2030; Panda-Freedom #1 Upgrade TBD->2031; Morgan-Outer Circle 230kV TBD->2030; Pinnacle Peak-Ocotillo rebuilds 2029->2030; Saguaro Power Campus 2029->2030; Cholla-Chevelon cut-in 2028->2029; Hashknife and Contrail 2025->2026; Four Corners-Cholla-Pinnacle Peak 345kV rebuilds 2037->2038.

Removed from the plan: Quartzsite-Colorado River 500kV Line, Komatke 230/69kV Substation (TBD table), Panda 230kV series reactor, 2 Pinnacle Peak 230kV series reactors (2026), Wafer 230kV STATCOM; Runway 230/69kV transformer additions moved from 2027 to TBD.

New TBD projects (no CEC filed): Hassayampa-North Gila 500kV #2 cut-in to Hoodoo Wash; TS37 500kV Lines; Texas Hill 500kV Switchyard and Lines; Morgan-Wafer 500kV #2 and 230kV #2; Jojoba-Independence 500kV #2; Watermelon-Jojoba 500kV #2 and #3; Independence-Saguaro 500kV Line.

Table 2 equipment 2026: Contrail 230/69 x3; Rudd 500/230 x1; Stratus 230/69 x1; Verde 230/69 replacements x2; shunt capacitors at Contrail, Raptor, Sabre (x2), Stratus; Cholla 500kV shunt reactor replacement; Country Club 230kV shunt reactors x2.

Table 2 equipment 2027: 230/69 transformers at Avery, Broadway, Diamond (x3), Freedom, Outer Circle, Scatter Wash; Sun Valley 500/230 x1; Broadway and Diamond 230kV capacitors; Komatke 230kV series reactor; Country Club-Meadowbrook 230kV UG upgrade (3 mi).

Table 2 equipment 2028: 230/69 transformers at Avery, Bianco (x2), Broadway, Ocotillo, Parkway, TS31 (x2), Yavapai; Mead Phoenix Project Q01 500/230 x1; Wafer 500/230 x3; capacitors at Avery (x2), TS31, Willow Lake (x2); Meadowbrook-Sunnyslope 230kV UG upgrade (5 mi).

Table 2 equipment 2029-2038: North Gila 500/230 and Rudd 500/230 (2029); Pinnacle Peak 230kV series reactors x3 (2029); Hazen 230/69 x2, Helios 230/69 x1, capacitors at Hazen and Independence (x2) (2030); Independence 500/230 x2 (2031); Cholla 345kV series capacitor replacements x2 (2038).

Table 2 TBD equipment: 230/69 transformers at Lone Peak, Meadowbrook, Palm Valley, Raceway, Runway (x4), Sun Valley, Trilby Wash, TS17 (x2), TS25 (x2), Wafer; TS37 500/69kV transformer; Runway 230kV capacitor; Country Club-Grand Terminal 230kV UG upgrade (2 mi); Surprise-El Sol 230kV reconductor (<1 mi).

Plan states compliance with NERC TPL-001-5.1 P0 and P1-P7; 13th BTA Decision 81541 (Oct 23, 2025) ordered a confidential congestion/load-growth-pocket report, which APS placed in the CEII Technical Study Report.

Phoenix area (APS+SRP) peak load 2020-2024: 13,279 / 13,115 / 13,054 / 13,551 / 13,906 MW; forecast 17,726 MW in 2030 and 19,650 MW in 2035; energy 58,007 GWh (2024) to 95,654 (2030) and 109,072 (2035); load factor rises from 48% to 61-63%.
findings.location: RMR Analysis Table 4, PDF p. 87 (report p. 23)

findings.statement: Phoenix RMR results: 2030 SIL 11,241 MW, peak 17,726, import at peak 11,368, RMR at peak 6,358 MW, 3,102 RMR hours, 5,518 GWh, $3.9M; 2035 SIL 15,181, peak 19,650, RMR at peak 6,218, 996 hours, 2,052 GWh, $1.8M; reserves 639 / 832 MW vs 439 / 429 required; no resources needed beyond the APS/SRP ten-year plans.
findings.location: RMR Table ES1 (PDF p. 70) and Table 3 (PDF p. 86)

findings.statement: Phoenix-area generation nameplate 8,184 MW: APS owned/purchased 2,435 MW (30%), SRP 5,750 MW (incl. 600 MW future). The Phoenix RMR study was triggered because the load forecast rose by more than 2.5%, driven largely by large loads in Maricopa County; Yuma was not triggered.

DG/EE study (2030 heavy summer): backing out incremental EE/DG adds 802 MW to APS load (EE 590 MW; Table 3 DG 212 MW) and 282 MW to SRP (EE 206, DG 76); no new APS or SRP overloads or voltage violations.

APS planning guidelines: nominal operating voltages 535/348/239/119 kV, continuous limits +/-5%, 8% maximum post-contingency voltage dip; standard new-line conductors 3x1780 ACSR Chukar or 2x2156 Bluebird (525 kV), 2x795 Tern (345 kV), 1x2156 ACSS Bluebird or 1x1272 Bittern (230 kV); new 230/69 transformers 113/150/188 MVA.

open_questions: RMR Table ES1 gives 2035 import at peak 11,432 MW but Table 3 gives 13,432 MW (19,650 - 13,432 = 6,218 RMR at peak); ES1 likely a typo.
DG/EE executive summary says 590 MW EE + 173 MW DG for APS, but Table 3 gives 212 MW DG (590 + 212 = 802 MW).
Desert Sun / Watermelon: which generator or queue position is behind the 'potential new power plant', and its MW?
Technical Study Report (congestion and load-growth pockets), Extreme Contingency Study and System Ratings are CEII, available only under a protective agreement.
Ratings are TBD for most 500kV projects (Jojoba-Rudd, Wafer, Hashknife, Snowflake); they must be assumed when modelling these projects in TARA cases.
